content.intro: In this lesson, you will study clustering Algorithms within Unsupervised, Self-Supervised, and Reinforcement Learning. You will connect the syllabus topics below to a small, inspectable example and practice stating what the evidence does—and does not—support.

content_blocks.title: The central idea
content_blocks.text: Clustering groups observations according to a chosen representation and distance or density rule. Results depend on scaling, algorithm assumptions, parameters, and the definition of a useful group.

content_blocks.title: A practical way to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with the task definition and the inputs available. Make the expected behavior explicit, choose a simple reference point, and inspect both ordinary examples and cases where assumptions may fail. Learning without direct labels and learning through reward solve different problems. Inspect what feedback is available and what success means.

content_blocks.code:
train = [0, 1, 1, 0]
validation = [0, 1]
baseline_prediction = max(set(train), key=train.count)
accuracy = sum(baseline_prediction == y for y in validation) / len(validation)
print("baseline accuracy:", round(accuracy, 2))

content_blocks.text: If the output differs, check indentation and spelling, confirm you saved the intended file, and compare each input value with the example. content.task: Try it yourself: build a tiny synthetic dataset for clustering algorithms, establish a simple baseline, and define a suitable metric before looking at results. Separate development decisions from final evaluation and describe one important error. The linked practice activity is: Cluster Analysis.
